text: sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 as Parquet through a three-stage pipeline connected by bounded channels. A **reader** process opens a Postgres cursor and streams rows in fixed-size batches, applying backpressure so it never outruns downstream consumers. Each batch is handed to a **converter**, which maps Postgres types to their Parquet equivalents and encodes the rows into columnar row groups, buffering until a target row-group size is reached. Completed row groups flow to an **uploader**, which assembles them into multipart S3 objects, issuing part uploads concurrently and retrying transient failures with exponential backoff before finalizing each object. Decoupling the stages lets slow network I/O overlap with CPU-bound encoding and database reads, so throughput is bounded by the slowest stage rather than their sum. Failures propagate through the channels, cancelling the pipeline cleanly.
